original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I \subset A$ be a finitely generated ideal.
There exists a right adjoint $R\Gamma_Z$ (\ref{equation-local-cohomology})
to the inclusion functor $D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A) \to D(A)$.
In fact, if $I$ is generated by $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in A$, then we have
$$
R\Gamma_Z(K) =
(A \to \prod\nolimits_{i_0} A_{f_{i_0}} \to
\prod\nolimits_{i_0 < i_1} A_{f_{i_0}f_{i_1}}
\to \ldots \to A_{f_1\ldots f_r}) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} K
$$
functorially in $K \in D(A)$.
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Then the functor $R\Gamma_Z:D(A)\to D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$ is **right adjoint** to the full inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$, and the displayed augmented Čech formula is a natural isomorphism for *every* $K\in D(A)$. The Čech construction and its augmentation $R\Gamma_Z(K)\to K$ are independent of the generating set in the derived category.
hypotheses: I finitely generated with f_i generators, full subcategory of complexes with power-torsion cohomology.
conclusions: The Čech tensor formula gives local cohomology and right adjunction.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-neighbourhood-extensions}
Let $A \to B$ be a flat ring map and let $I \subset A$ be a
finitely generated ideal such that $A/I \to B/IB$ is an isomorphism.
For $K \in D_{I^\infty\text{-torsion}}(A)$ and $L \in D(A)$
the map
$$
R\Hom_A(K, L) \longrightarrow R\Hom_B(K \otimes_A B, L \otimes_A B)
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. In particular, if $M$, $N$ are $A$-modules and
$M$ is $I$-power torsion, then the canonical map
$$
\Ext^i_A(M, N)
\longrightarrow
\Ext^i_B(M \otimes_A B, N \otimes_A B)
$$
is an isomorphism for all $i$.
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Let $A\to B$ be flat with $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}B/IB$. If $K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$ and $L\in D(A)$, then the canonical map
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(K\otimes_AB,L\otimes_AB)
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism of underlying derived complexes of abelian groups (equivalently of $A$-modules by restriction on the right). In particular, for $A$-modules $M,N$ with $M$ $I$-power torsion, $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}_B^i(M\otimes_AB,N\otimes_AB)$ for every $i\ge0$. Flatness allows ordinary tensor rather than derived tensor on modules.
hypotheses: A→B flat with A/I≈B/IB; K torsion-cohomology and L arbitrary.
conclusions: Derived Hom comparison and all Ext^i base-change maps are isomorphisms.
